Surah al-Ahqaf (The Sand Dunes) [Meccan, except verses 10, 15 and 35, which are Medinan; its verses are 34 or 35]

﴿Ha Mim﴾ God knows best what He means by it.
﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, the Qur'an, is the mubtada' (subject of the nominal sentence), ﴿from Allah﴾ is its khabar (predicate), ﴿the Almighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His creation.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 46, verse 3:

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except﴾ with creation ﴿in truth﴾, so that it would indicate Our power and Our oneness, ﴿and for a specified term﴾ until their annihilation on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned﴾ of, i.e., the punishment they are made to fear.

Say: ﴿Have you considered?﴾ Tell me ﴿what you invoke﴾, that is, worship, ﴿besides Allah﴾, namely the idols, (﴿what﴾ being the first object). ﴿Show me﴾, tell me, (﴿what﴾ is an emphatic repetition) ﴿what they have created﴾ (﴿what﴾ here is the second object) ﴿of the earth﴾ (﴿of﴾ specifies the ﴿what﴾). ﴿Or do they have a share﴾ (a partnership) ﴿in﴾ the creation of ﴿the heavens﴾ alongside Allah? (The particle ﴿أم﴾ (am, "or") here carries the meaning of the interrogative hamzah of denial.) ﴿Bring me a Book﴾ revealed ﴿before this﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿or some remnant﴾, that is, a remainder, ﴿of knowledge﴾ transmitted from the earlier people, which would confirm the truth of your claim in worshipping idols, that they bring you closer to Allah, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 5:

﴿And who⁠ ﴾ is an interrogative used in the sense of negation, meaning: no one [is] ﴿more astray than one who calls upon﴾ worships ﴿other than Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection﴾. They are the idols, which never respond to their worshippers with anything they ask for. ﴿And they are heedless of their calling﴾, i.e., their worship, ﴿because they are inanimate and do not comprehend.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 6:

﴿And when mankind are gathered together, they [the idols] will be enemies to them [their worshippers], and they will deny their worship.﴾ That is, the idols [will be] enemies to their worshippers, and they will be disbelievers in, i.e., deniers of, the worship of their worshippers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 7:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, clear as they are,﴾ i.e., the people of Mecca, ﴿Our verses﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾ manifest, ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ among them ﴿say of the truth﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿when it has come to them: "This is evident sorcery."﴾ clear, manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 8:

[Am] means "bal" (rather), with the interrogative hamza of denial. ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is, the Qur'an. ﴿Say: If I have invented it﴾ supposing so, ﴿then you cannot avail me anything against Allah﴾ that is, against His punishment; ﴿you cannot avert from me any of the punishment of Allah if Allah should punish me﴾ ﴿He is most knowing of what you say concerning it﴾ about the Qur'an. ﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ Exalted is He. ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ to whoever repents, ﴿and so He does not hasten punishment upon you﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 9:

﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾ (badīʿan, i.e., new or unprecedented), meaning: I am not the first messenger, for many messengers came before me, so why do you deny me? ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ in the world: will I be expelled from my land, or killed as the prophets before me were killed, or will you stone me, or will you be swallowed up by the earth as the deniers before you were? ﴿I only follow﴾ (in) ﴿what is revealed to me﴾, meaning the Qur'an, and I do not innovate anything of my own accord. ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾, one whose warning is evident.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 10:

﴿Say: Have you considered?﴾ Tell me, what is your state ﴿if it [the Qur'an] is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it﴾ — a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya) — ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to its like﴾ — he is ʿAbdullah ibn Salam — ﴿concerning its like﴾, i.e., testified to the fact that it is from Allah ﴿and believed﴾ — the witness — ﴿while you were arrogant﴾, you were too proud to believe. The answer to the conditional (jawab al-shart) is what is joined to it by ʿaṭf: "Are you not wrongdoers?" — indicated by what follows: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

﴿And those who disbelieved said of those who believed﴾ — that is, concerning them — ﴿"Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they are not guided by it"﴾ — that is, those who say this — ﴿"by it"﴾ — that is, the Qur'an — ﴿"they will say, 'This is an old lie.'"﴾ — that is, the Qur'an — ﴿"an old lie"﴾ — a lie.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 12:

﴿And before it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿was the Book of Musa﴾, i.e., the Torah, ﴿as a guide and a mercy﴾ to those who believe in it; these are two circumstantial states (ḥālān). ﴿And this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a Book confirming﴾ the books before it, ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾, a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the pronoun in "confirming"; ﴿to warn those who have done wrong﴾, i.e., the polytheists of Makkah, ﴿and as good tidings for the doers of good﴾, i.e., the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 13:

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ upon obedience.

﴿Those are the companions of the Garden, abiding therein﴾. ﴿Abiding﴾ (خالِدِينَ, khālidīna) is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, a word describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). ﴿A recompense﴾ (جَزاءً, jazā'an) is in the accusative as a *maṣdar* (verbal noun), governed by its implied verb, meaning: they are being recompensed (يُجْزَوْنَ, yujzawna).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 46, verse 15:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man (goodness) to his parents﴾. And in another reading, *iḥsānan* (كُرْهًا) means: We commanded him to be good to them. So *iḥsānan* is in the accusative as a **maṣdar** (verbal noun, *maṣdar*) governed by its implied verb, and similarly *ḥasanan*. ﴿His mother carried him in hardship and bore him in hardship﴾, meaning with difficulty. ﴿And his carrying and weaning﴾ from suckling ﴿is thirty months﴾: six months is the minimum period of pregnancy, and the remainder is the maximum period of suckling. It was said that if she conceived him and he was six or nine (months), she nursed him for the rest. ﴿Until﴾ is the end point of an implied clause, meaning: and he lived until ﴿when he reaches his full strength﴾, which is the completion of his power, intellect and judgment, at least thirty-three years, or thirty. ﴿And reaches forty years﴾, meaning its completion, and this is the greater part of *ashudd* (full maturity). ﴿He says, "My Lord…"﴾ etc. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he reached forty years, two years after the Prophet's ﷺ mission. He believed in him, then his parents believed, then his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and the son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was Abu ʿAtiq. ﴿Inspire me﴾, meaning guide me ﴿to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed﴾ with them ﴿upon me and upon my parents﴾, which is monotheism ﴿and to do righteousness that You will accept﴾. So he freed nine of the believers who were being tortured for God's sake. ﴿And make righteous for me my offspring﴾, and all of them were believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 16:

﴿Those﴾ i.e., those who say this statement: Abu Bakr and others, ﴿for whom We accept the best of what they did﴾ with the meaning of "good," ﴿and overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise﴾ as a circumstantial clause, i.e., being among them ﴿—a true promise which they were promised﴾ in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 17:

﴿And the one who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?"﴾ In another recitation the two letters are assimilated (idgham), and the word is intended in the generic sense (al-jins). ﴿Uff﴾ is pronounced with the fa' kasra or fatha, and is in the sense of a verbal noun, meaning stench and foulness. ﴿To you both﴾: I am disgusted with you both. ﴿Do you promise me﴾ (in another recitation with idgham) ﴿that I will be brought forth﴾ from the grave? ﴿When generations have passed﴾, nations ﴿before me﴾, and they did not come out of the graves. ﴿And both of them call upon God for help﴾, asking Him for relief by his return, and saying, if you do not return, ﴿woe to you﴾, meaning your destruction, in the sense of "you have been destroyed". ﴿Believe﴾ in resurrection. ﴿Indeed, the promise of God is true,﴾ ﴿but he says, "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients"﴾, meaning their falsehoods.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 18:

﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has been justified﴾ meaning it has become due (wajaba), ﴿upon them, [the word]﴾ of punishment.

﴿And for each﴾ of the kind of the believer and the disbeliever, ﴿there are degrees﴾. So the degrees of the believers in Paradise are high, and the degrees of the disbelievers in the Fire are low. ﴿According to what they did﴾, i.e., the believers from acts of obedience (ṭāʿāt) and the disbelievers from acts of disobedience (maʿāṣī). ﴿And that He may pay them in full﴾, i.e., Allah. In one recitation (qirāʾah), it is read with the nūn. ﴿Their deeds﴾, i.e., their recompense, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ in anything, meaning that nothing is reduced for the believers or increased for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 20:

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire﴾ by having it uncovered for them, it will be said to them: ﴿You used up your good things﴾ — read with one hamza, with two hamzas, with one hamza and a madd, with both (the two readings just listed), and with the second hamza made easy (tashil) — ﴿in your worldly life, by your occupation with your pleasures﴾ ﴿and you enjoyed them﴾ meaning you took your enjoyment of them. ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾ meaning the disgrace ﴿for what you were arrogant about﴾ meaning you were proud ﴿in the earth without right, and for what you used to defy (tafsuqun)﴾ by it, and you will be punished by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 21:

﴿And mention the brother of ʿĀd﴾ — he is Hūd, peace be upon him. ﴿When﴾ — this is a substitution of partial inclusion (badal ishtimal) for the preceding phrase. ﴿He warned his people﴾ — he frightened them ﴿in al-Aḥqāf﴾ — a valley in Yemen where their dwellings were. ﴿And warners had already passed﴾ — messengers had gone ﴿before him and after him﴾ — that is, before Hūd and after him, to their peoples. ﴿Saying﴾ — that is, that he said: ﴿Worship none but Allah﴾. The clause ﴿And warners had already passed﴾ is a parenthetical insertion (iʿtiraḍ). ﴿Indeed, I fear for you﴾ — if you worship other than Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 46, verse 22:

﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful."﴾

(To turn us away) from worshipping them. (So bring us what you threaten us with) of punishment for worshipping them. (If you are of the truthful) in claiming that it will come to us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 23:

﴿Hud said﴾ [i.e., Hud said], ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah"﴾ — He it is who knows when the punishment will come to you. ﴿And I convey to you what I have been sent with﴾ to you, ﴿but I see you to be a people who are ignorant﴾ by your hastening of the punishment.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 46, verse 24:

﴿Then when they saw it﴾ i.e., what was the punishment, ﴿as a cloud﴾ a cloud that appeared on the horizon of the sky, ﴿coming towards their valleys, they said: "This is a cloud that will bring us rain."﴾ i.e., bringing rain to us. ﴿Nay, it is that which you were hastening [for]﴾ of the punishment, ﴿a wind﴾ a substitute for "that," ﴿wherein is a painful punishment﴾ causing pain.

﴿Tudammir﴾ (destroys) ﴿kulla shay'in﴾ (everything) ﴿marrat 'alayhi﴾ (it passed over) ﴿bi-amri rabbihā﴾ (by the command of its Lord), that is, by His will, meaning: everything He willed to destroy with it. So it destroyed their men, their women, their children and their property, by lifting them up between the sky and the earth and tearing them apart. Hud and those who believed with him were spared. ﴿Fa-asbahū lā yurā illā masākinuhum﴾ (So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings). ﴿Kadhālika﴾ (Thus), as We recompensed them, ﴿najzi al-qawma al-mujrimīn﴾ (We recompense the criminal people), other than them.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 46, verse 26:**

﴿And We had established them in that wherein﴾: "in that which" (*fi alladhi*). "*In*" (*in*) is either negating (*nafiyya*, meaning "not") or superfluous (*za'ida*, meaning "extra," adding emphasis without changing sense). ﴿We had established you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿in it﴾, meaning in strength and wealth. ﴿And We made for them hearing﴾, in the sense of hearing faculties (*asma'an*, plural). ﴿And sight and hearts﴾, meaning hearts. ﴿But their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts, at all﴾, meaning, not at all. "*Min shay'*" ("at all") is literally "anything," and "*min*" here is superfluous. ﴿Since﴾ (*idh*) is governed by *aghna* ("avail") and has taken on the meaning of causality (*ta'lil*): ﴿they used to deny the signs of God﴾, meaning His clear proofs. ﴿And there encompassed them﴾, meaning descended upon them, ﴿that which they used to mock﴾, meaning the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 27:

﴿And We had certainly destroyed the towns around you﴾, i.e., their inhabitants, like Thamud and ʿAd and the people of Lut. ﴿And We diversified the signs﴾, i.e., We repeated the clear proofs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 28:

﴿Why then did they not⌋ help them⌋ — hallā (why not, would that) — ﴿nasarahum﴾ (help them) by repelling the punishment from them ﴿those whom they had taken as objects of worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿as means of nearness﴾, through which they drew near to Allah, ﴿as gods besides Him﴾, and they are the idols. The first object of ittakhadha (took) is a pronoun, omitted, referring back to the relative pronoun, i.e., "they"; and the second object, qurbānan (as means of nearness), and ālihah (gods) is a substitute (badal) for it. ﴿Rather, they strayed⌋ — ḍallū (were lost, went astray) — ﴿from them﴾ at the descent of the punishment. ﴿And that⌋ — i.e., their taking the idols as gods and as means of nearness — ﴿was their falsehood⌋ — ifkuhum (their lie) — ﴿and what they used to fabricate﴾ — yaftarūna (they used to lie). Here mā is either a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah) or a relative pronoun, and its returning pronoun is omitted, i.e., "in it" (fīh).

(And mention) when We inclined toward you a company of jinn (﴿إذْ صَرَفْنا إلَيْك نَفَرًا مِن الجِنّ﴾), listening to the Qur'an. They were the jinn of Nasibin in Yemen, or the jinn of Nineveh, and they numbered seven or nine. (The Prophet (ﷺ) was at Batn Nakhl, leading his Companions in the dawn prayer.) Narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿فَلَمّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا﴾ (When they were present at it, they said), meaning some of them said to others, ﴿أنْصِتُوا﴾ (Be silent), listen attentively to its recitation. ﴿فَلَمّا قُضِيَ﴾ (When it was finished), meaning when its recitation was completed, ﴿ولَّوْا﴾ (they turned back) ﴿إلى قَوْمهمْ مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ (to their people as warners), warning their people of punishment if they did not believe. They had been Jews, and they had (since) embraced Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 46, verse 30:

﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book"﴾ that is the Qur'an, ﴿"revealed after Moses, confirming what is before it"﴾ i.e., what precedes it, such as al-Tawrah (the Torah), ﴿"guiding to the truth"﴾ Islam, ﴿"and to a straight path"﴾ i.e., its path.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 31:

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), to faith, ﴿and believe in him; He will forgive﴾ Allah will forgive ﴿you of your sins﴾ i.e., some of them, because among them are wrongs (mazalim), which are not forgiven except with the consent of their owners, ﴿and protect you from a painful punishment﴾ painful, causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 32:

﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth﴾, i.e., he cannot escape Allah by fleeing from Him so that he eludes Him. ﴿And he will not have for him﴾, for whoever does not respond, ﴿any protectors other than Him﴾, i.e., other than Allah, ﴿who could ward off the punishment from him﴾. ﴿Those﴾, who did not respond, ﴿are in manifest error﴾, clear and evident.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 46, verse 33:

﴿Do they not see﴾ i.e., know, [that is,] those who deny the Resurrection, ﴿that God, who created the heavens and the earth, and did not tire in creating them﴾ i.e., was not incapable of it, ﴿is able﴾ (bi-qadir) — the predicate of "anna" (that), and the "bi" has been added to it because the sentence has the force of "Is not God able...?" ﴿to give life to the dead? Yes!﴾ He is able to bring the dead back to life.
﴿And the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾, by being made to suffer in it. It will be said to them: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ [i.e., is this punishment not real?]

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 46, verse 35:

﴿So be patient﴾ over the harm from your people, ﴿as the steadfast of resolve (ulu al-'azm) were patient﴾, those possessing steadfastness and endurance in the face of hardships, ﴿among the Messengers﴾ before you, so that you become one of them with resolve. Here "min" (مِن) is *li-l-bayan* (explanatory, indicating the category), so that all of them are possessors of resolve. It has also been said that "min" is *li-l-tab'id* (partitive), so Adam is not among them, because of His Exalted saying, ﴿And We did not find in him resolve﴾, nor Yunus, because of His Exalted saying, ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾.

﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾, i.e., for your people, the descent of the punishment upon them. It has been said that he became impatient with them, so he wished for the punishment to descend upon them, and so he was commanded to be patient and to refrain from seeking to hasten the punishment, for it is surely coming.

﴿As if they, on the Day they see what they are promised﴾ of punishment in the Hereafter, because of its length, ﴿they had not remained﴾ in the world, in their assumption. ﴿[This is] a message﴾: this Qur'an is a conveyance from God to you. ﴿So will be destroyed﴾, i.e., no, ﴿except the people who are defiant﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, at the sight of the punishment.
